newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia '97 net grain output may fall to 60 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia '97 net grain output may fall to 60 mln T.

text.p: Russia's net 1997 grain harvest may be no higher than 60.0 million tonnes compared with the 69.3 million produced in 1996, a research institute said on Wednesday.

Interfax news agency quoted the All-Russian Scientific Research Institute for Agricultural Economics as saying the Agriculture Ministry's target of a net grain harvest of 70 million tonnes this year was "highly doubtful".

The main reason given for the expected fall in output this year was low winter sowings. Analysts taking part in the study said the area sown to winter crops was 13.0 million hectares for this year's crop against 14.2 million last year.
Lower winter kill levels in 1997 than in 1996 could not compensate for the sharp fall in sowings, the institute's study was quoted as saying.
Some agricultural analysts have said it is still too early to accurately forecast the size of the 1997 net grain crop.
But a document from the Institute of Agricultural Information and Technical-Economic Investigations said last month that net 1997 grain output might be 63.0 million tonnes.
Russia produced 63.4 million tonnes of grain in 1995. The 1995 and 1996 crops were the worst on record in three decades.
